claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element, nearly equiatomic automotive alloy catalyst with low platinum-group-metal content.
The starting catalyst suffers activity loss and durability limitations during exposure to H2O, NO, and thermal aging.
Depositing a 2–3 nm CeO2 or Ce–Zr mixed-oxide overlayer by ALD will significantly improve catalytic activity retention and durability.
The oxide-overlayer intervention will maintain low platinum-group-metal consumption.
ALD at 150–250 °C with optimized pulse durations and precursor exposure can produce a conformal, porous coating without changing the bulk alloy structure.
The ALD treatment will form a conformal nanometer-thick oxide overlayer that partially encapsulates the catalyst particles.
The oxide overlayer will physically protect the catalyst particles.
The oxide overlayer will introduce surface oxygen-storage capacity.
The ultrathin oxide layer will act as a barrier against catalyst sintering.
The ultrathin oxide layer will inhibit chemical degradation caused by H2O and NO.
Enhanced oxygen storage and release will facilitate dynamic redox cycles.
The proposed dynamic redox cycles will stabilize active sites during thermal aging and transient exhaust operation.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the coated catalyst will retain higher catalytic activity over time.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the coated catalyst will show greater resistance to deactivation and sintering under transient low-temperature exhaust conditions.
The expected benefits apply to low-temperature transient gasoline and hybrid-vehicle exhaust conditions, whereas performance at extreme high temperature is untested.
Increasing overlayer protection may reduce reactant access to active sites, so performance will depend on ALD process optimization.
